name: MonarchShiftRoster
title: ShiftRoster
wrapsNative: Menu with an inline Picker (.pickerStyle(.inline)) and a Clear Button per cell, MonarchTabs (one day or one person at a time), ViewThatFits choosing between the grid and the day layout, ScrollView(.horizontal) for a forced grid, MonarchEventChip(variant: .bar), MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchBanner, MonarchEmptyState, .redacted(reason: .placeholder) while loading, Date.FormatStyle
summary: Who works which shift on which day: a shift, a day off or nothing for each person and day of a range, with hours per person and the number of people working per day, edited from a system menu on each cell.
whenToUse: For a team's weekly or fortnightly rota in a workforce or attendance screen, where a manager assigns shifts and reads coverage per day. Save each MonarchShiftRosterChange in onChange.
whenNotToUse: For meetings or appointments use MonarchAgendaList. For one person's own upcoming shifts use MonarchAgendaList. For bulk rotations or copying a week, build the product's own sheet; the roster edits one cell at a time.
api: init(members: [MonarchShiftRosterMember], shifts: [MonarchShiftRosterShift], from: Date, value: Binding<[String: [Date: MonarchShiftRosterAssignment]]>, days: Int = 7, layout: MonarchShiftRosterLayout = .automatic, isReadOnly: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, showsTotals: Bool = true, today: Date? = Date(), calendar: Calendar = .current, uses24HourClock: Bool? = nil, error: String? = nil, labels: MonarchShiftRosterLabels = MonarchShiftRosterLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchShiftRosterChange) -> Void)? = nil, onSelectMember: (@MainActor (MonarchShiftRosterMember) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchShiftRosterShift { init(id: String, name: String, start: Int, end: Int, shortName: String? = nil, color: Color? = nil) }
struct MonarchShiftRosterMember { init(id: String, name: String, description: String? = nil, image: Image? = nil, avatarURL: URL? = nil) }
struct MonarchShiftRosterChange { init(memberId: String, day: Date, assignment: MonarchShiftRosterAssignment?) }
enum MonarchShiftRosterLayout { case automatic, grid, byDay, byPerson }

struct MonarchShiftRosterLabels { init(roster: String? = nil, person: String? = nil, day: String? = nil, off: String? = nil, unassigned: String? = nil, clear: String? = nil, menuTitle: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, cell: (@Sendable (String, String, String) -> String)? = nil, range: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, overnight: String? = nil, hours: String? = nil, hoursValue: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, working: String? = nil, workingValue: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, today: String? = nil, emptyTitle: String? = nil, emptyDescription: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil) }

options.name: members
options.description: The people in display order, each with an id, a name, an optional description line and an optional picture (Image or avatarURL).

options.name: shifts
options.description: The shifts in menu order: id, name, start and end in minutes from midnight (an end at or before the start ends the next day), an optional short name for the grid and an optional colour.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day shown: any time on that day in calendar.

options.name: value
options.description: Assignments by member id, then by any time on the day: .shift(id) or .off. A missing day is not assigned.

options.name: days
options.description: How many days to show from from, clamped to 1 to 62.

options.name: layout
options.description: .grid (people by days), .byDay (tabs of days, a row per person), .byPerson (tabs of people, a row per day), or .automatic: the grid when every column fits and the text is at most xxLarge, otherwise .byDay.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a redacted placeholder, read as "Loading roster", instead of the roster.

options.name: showsTotals
options.description: Shows each person's hours over the range and the number of people working per day.

options.name: today
options.description: The day marked Today, read in calendar; nil for no marker. The day layout opens on it when it is in the range. Pass a fixed date in tests and previews.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone days are read and formatted in.

options.name: uses24HourClock
options.description: Shows shift times on a 24-hour clock (true) or a 12-hour clock (false). nil follows the environment's locale.

options.name: error
options.description: A message shown in a danger MonarchBanner instead of the roster.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called after value changes, with the member id, the start of the day and the new assignment (nil when cleared), so the app can save it.

options.name: onSelectMember
options.description: Makes each person a button, for example to open their schedule on a detail screen.

options.name: empty
options.description: Replaces the built-in empty state shown when members is empty.

states.name: shift
states.description: A MonarchEventChip bar in the shift's colour with the name (the short name in the grid) and the times.

states.name: off
states.description: A muted fill with the word Off.

states.name: not assigned
states.description: A dashed outline with "Not assigned" (a dash in the narrow grid cells; VoiceOver still reads "Not assigned").

states.name: today
states.description: Today's tab reads "Today"; the day heading and grid header use the strong accent, with an info badge or the word Today.

states.name: menu open
states.description: A system menu headed by the person and the day, with a checkable item per shift, Off, and Clear when the day is assigned.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) the cells keep their look but cannot be opened; VoiceOver reads them as dimmed. Tabs are disabled too.

states.name: loading
states.description: Redacted placeholder rows replace the roster.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with the app's message replaces the roster.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no people, an empty state (or the app's empty view) replaces the roster.

appearance: Rows are separated by the subtle divider; names are in the default text colour and descriptions, hours and counts in the muted colour. A shift cell keeps the event chip's colours (the shift colour only as the bar and a light tint), a day off uses the muted background, and an unassigned day a dashed default border. Today uses the strong accent and an info badge. The grid's header and footer rows sit on the subtle background. High contrast themes use their own roles; every state is also written.
platformNotes: The web ShiftRoster is always a table of people by days with a roving-focus keyboard grid and Delete to clear. On a phone that table does not fit, so iOS shows one day at a time with a MonarchTabs strip (or one person at a time) and keeps the table for an iPad or a wide window (automatic picks it through ViewThatFits when every column fits). Each cell is a system Menu with an inline Picker, so the current choice is checked and VoiceOver, the keyboard and pointer work as in any iOS menu; the web's arrow-key grid navigation is not reproduced. The web takes ISO dates, a BCP 47 locale and an hour cycle; iOS takes Date values matched in a Calendar, the environment's locale and uses24HourClock. Android names the same types and options (members, shifts, from, value, days, layout, readOnly, loading, showTotals, today, is24Hour, error, onMemberClick, labels, empty); iOS follows SwiftUI conventions: the value is a Binding with onChange reporting each MonarchShiftRosterChange, the flags are isReadOnly, isLoading, showsTotals and uses24HourClock, onMemberClick is onSelectMember, and enabled is the environment's .disabled(_:). The plan's drag to assign is not offered on any platform: the web has no drag either, and a menu per cell is the touch and VoiceOver pattern. Day tabs show one line ("Wed 4" or "Today") because MonarchTabs labels are one line; Android shows the weekday above the date. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook iOS app. Several closures are optional (onChange, onSelectMember). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onChange.
accessibility: Each editable cell is a system Menu, one element with a touch target of at least 44 points, named "<person>, <day>: <assignment>", for example "Alex Kim, Tuesday, November 3, Today: Night, N, 22:00 to 06:00, overnight"; the short name is added only in the grid, where it is what is shown.
The cell's menu is headed by the person and the day; the current choice is checked by the system Picker, and each shift is read with its spoken time range.
Read-only cells are one element with the same name and no action; with .disabled(true) cells are read as dimmed.
Day and person tabs are a MonarchTabs strip named "Day" or "Person"; the selected tab has the selected trait.
The day's date under the tabs is a header read with "Today" for today; after an assignment the new number working is announced.
Each person is one element read as "name, description, Hours: total"; with onSelectMember it is a button with a 44-point target.

The grid is a container named "Shift roster"; day headers are headers read as the full date, the hours column is read as "Hours: 40 h" and footer counts with the date, "Wednesday, November 4: 3 working".
Avatars are decorative; no state is shown by colour alone.
At the accessibility text sizes the cell moves under the person or day so no text is cut, and the automatic layout never shows the grid above xxLarge; grid columns scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Keys in value may be any time on the day; they are matched in calendar, and a change replaces any key on that day with the start of the day.
An assignment to a shift id that is not among shifts reads as not assigned and counts no hours.
A shift whose end equals its start lasts 24 hours and is overnight.
Choosing the current assignment again changes nothing and calls no onChange.
Hours are rounded to one decimal in the locale's number format.
Shift times are formatted on a fixed UTC day, so a daylight-saving change in calendar does not move them.
The roster does not scroll vertically; put it in a scrolling screen. The grid scrolls sideways when forced with layout: .grid.
Long names and descriptions wrap; nothing is truncated.
